newsitem.title: UK: SHELL SEES 97 CAPEX SLIGHTLY BELOW TARGET.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SEES 97 CAPEX SLIGHTLY BELOW TARGET.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group Group said it would step up its capital expenditure in the second half of the year but added total spending was expected to remain slightly below the full 1997 target.
Capital expenditure and exploration expense for the 1997 second quarter was 1.7 billion stg. This was 16 percent lower than a year ago due to reductions in the refining and chemicals sector.
Spending will notably rise in the exploration and production sector, particularly for projects in Egypt and Oman, Shell Transport and Trading chairman Mark Moody-Stuart said.
"But it (total spending) may not fully meet our full-year capital expenditure targets," he added.
Problems in getting several government approvals and licences were to blame, Moody Stuart said.
He also pointed to Nigeria, where Shell's spending is restricted by government delays in funding its joint venture exploration programmes.
